name: Stig
tagline: Tagged's social-scale graph-oriented database with causal time travel and a compiled Stigscript language.
description: Stig was built at the social network Tagged between 2010 and 2014 to give applications a single path to data and drop the memcache-plus-MySQL layer. Its ideas were unusual: Points of View are optimistic, isolated workspaces that merge into a global view; the Flux Capacitor keeps a causality-ordered history so you can do consistent reads at any point in time; and Stigscript is a compiled, type-safe functional language, with compile-time unit tests, whose packages compile to shared libraries loaded by the server. It ran as a single node with failover and replication on its own block device, with sharding still on the drawing board. Tagged released it under Apache 2.0, but development ended; the only public copy is a 2019 archive repository.
statusNote: Developed at Tagged 2010-2014 and open-sourced under Apache 2.0, then abandoned; the only public copy is a 2019 archive repo. Use Neo4j, Memgraph or FoundationDB.

scale.notes: Single node with failover replication; a sharded design was planned but not delivered.

strengths: Causality-ordered history allows consistent reads at any point in time
Points of View give optimistic, isolated workspaces that merge back
Compiled, type-safe query language with compile-time unit tests
Back end was used in production at a large social network
weaknesses: Abandoned; no releases, maintainers or community
Linux only and needs a dedicated block device
Front end and tooling were never finished
No sharding despite the scale ambitions
useCases: Studying causal versioning and time-travel designs
Reference for compiled query languages in databases
